text: Ryanair is cutting a million passenger seats in Spain. In related news, they're adding 1 million standing-room tickets at half the price and twice the indignity.

The 17th-century painting resurfaced after 80 years but wasn't available for long, which makes sense because in 2024 apparently everything has to be a limited drop. Museums are really out here treating repatriated Nazi loot like it's a Supreme collab.

The childcare task force's spotlight keeps revealing the discouraging 3.7-kilometer distance to the implementation office, so analysts now conduct their reviews while facing backward. Optimism improves when you can't see how far you need to walk.

Experts placed body wipes on a scale to weigh in, concluding that any wipe under 1.7 ounces lacks the gravitational pull necessary to attract dirt particles. The American Hygiene Board has now mandated that all effective cleaning products must achieve "measurable downward force."

Netflix asking if something is "an exercise in narcissism" is like a mirror factory asking if you've been checking your reflection too much. This is the platform that greenlit a documentary about making The Crown, then made a behind-the-scenes special about filming that documentary.

Colleges are welcoming pets to reduce students' stress, which is very effective since nothing makes you forget about your failing grade like discovering what a dog can do to a textbook in under three minutes.

Taipei City Council is in the dog house after buying a Chinese-made patrol robot. They wanted surveillance technology to monitor the streets, but the only thing getting watched now is their bank account—by very angry taxpayers.

The Bureau of Meteorology has issued warnings about severe weather barreling towards the south and a wet spring ahead. Forecasters confirmed they meant the season, not their prediction that the office slinky would get dunked in the break room sink by Ted again.

Nonalcoholic beer and mocktails prove that humans need props more than intoxication. We've literally invented fake alcohol so we can keep doing the hand-holding part of drinking without the drinking part, like a security blanket made of hops.

Massachusetts cranberry bogs are transitioning to vibrant wetlands, marking their official entry into the gig economy where they'll work flexible hours as habitats. The bogs report feeling less pressure now that they're no longer expected to produce Thanksgiving dinner every single year.

After their U.S. Open match, Ostapenko and Townsend got into a heated post-match row that required Coast Guard intervention. The USTA has since clarified that "rowing it out" was intended as a figure of speech and apologized for the venue's proximity to navigable waterways.
Humans inhale 68,000 microplastic particles daily according to a new study, making it the only diet where we're actually overachieving our goals. If only paying rent came this naturally.
